Diego: Hey all — 1st week here. Trying to follow the runtime build README on my company Windows laptop (WSL2). Container starts but link fails: `cannot find -lcuda` and `modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found`. Any onboarding tips?

Diego: run command I used:
```bash
docker run --gpus all -v /mnt/c/Users/diego/src:/src -w /src redwood/dev:cuda-12.1 make -j12
[ 10%] Linking CXX executable llm_serving
/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lcuda
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found
```

Mika: welcome! :wave: that modprobe error usually means the host kernel module (nvidia) didn't load — often DKMS failed at driver install or Secure Boot blocked unsigned modules. What does `dmesg | grep -i nvidia` on Windows WSL host show (run in an elevated PowerShell: wsl -d <distro> -- dmesg)?

Diego: ran dmesg in WSL, seeing `nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout` and `nvidia_dkms: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing`.

Natanael: yeah that confirms it — Secure Boot prevented the DKMS-installed kernel module from loading. Two options: (1) use our cloud onboarding GPU instance (recommended if you can't change BIOS), or (2) enroll a signed module: infra has a signing key and process to sign modules for company laptops. Ping infra.

Rosie: also check Windows Device Manager for NVIDIA driver installation method — if drivers were installed manually (not via our internal repo) DKMS might not have been used and WSL may not expose the driver. For WSL2 we require the NVIDIA WSL driver (signed) and Windows feature updates.

Diego: I don't have BIOS access to disable Secure Boot. I'd prefer not to change firmware. How do I get access to the cloud dev GPU?

Mika: file a quick infra request describing you need onboarding GPU access and link to this thread. We have a small pool `onboard-gpu-{1..3}`. infra will add your SSH key and a short runbook. I'll cc infra.

Natanael: short-term workaround: you can build with `-DUSE_CUDA=OFF` locally to run unit tests, or use `redwood/dev:cpu-debug` image. But for integration tests and performance checks you'll need one of those GPU boxes.

Diego: I tried `-DUSE_CUDA=OFF`, build completes but later tests fail because some CI fixtures call into a prebuilt plugin expecting CUDA symbols (LTO undefined refs). Any way to skip those tests?

Rosie: run `ctest -R unit -E gpu` to run only non-GPU tests locally. For the plugin, you can set `-DBUILD_TELEMETRY=OFF` during cmake to avoid linking the GPU-only plugin.

infra-bot: INFRA-520 opened: "Onboard GPU access + signed module flow for Secure Boot laptops". Assigned to infra oncall.

Diego: thanks — filing the infra request now. Will run unit tests locally and grab GPU access for integration. Ill add a note to the onboarding doc about Secure Boot and DKMS. Tagging @Mika @Natanael if I hit infra delays. :thumbsup:
